reachable: Yes, fully reachable, and I checked by executing the module against the real training data rather than by reading. The batcher is an upstream data-distribution mechanism with no parameters of its own, so "receives gradient" does not apply to it directly; what matters is whether it changes the gradient stream, and it demonstrably does. harness.py:78-83 calls `next_batch(step, steps)` every training step and collates exactly the returned indices into the batch that produces the loss; the returned index multiset is what determines the in-batch negative pool for r12_antiretrieval_ring_negatives (a listwise softmax over every cmd position in the batch). I loaded the real encoded train cache (data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd/emb-seq-train.pt), applied M.standardize_stats/apply_stats and M.split_train_dev(seed=0) exactly as eval/adapter.py:186 does, giving the same 2304-sequence fit the scorer will use, and ran make_batcher on it with the genome's exact params. It produced batches whose depth composition differs enormously from uniform (mean drawn depth 5.38 vs 2.33), so the mechanism reaches the loss with a large effect size. Contract compliance verified on 1200 batches: exactly 64 indices, all in range, 0 violations; bit-for-bit deterministic on re-instantiation with the same seed; fit never mutated (all z_cmd/z_obs/cmds/image compared before and after); global torch RNG state unchanged. Cost is not a barrier: setup 0.051 s and 113 microseconds per batch on 2304 sequences. One caveat on reachability of the SECOND claimed mechanism: the collision pools are built and are of high quality (I dumped a real pool of 17 trajectories that all end in `cat /tmp/w/cups/usr/share/misc/magic.txt.5` with 17 different canary contents, verified against the raw output text in train.jsonl), but at the shipped alpha_max=2.5 the depth tilt collapses them before they reach the loss, so that mechanism is largely inert in the configuration that will be scored — see divergence 1.
summary: The code is correct, cheap, contract-clean, and its central novel primitive is exactly as advertised and verified against ground truth. The mv-reachability walk reproduces meta["cups"]["depth"] on 24/24 jail sequences with the exact depth histogram the hypothesis states (1:4, 2:8, 3:4, 4:5, 5:2, 6:1) and the exact "6 of 27 routed-read paths recur" figure, and the read-collision pools are real: I dumped a pool of 17 trajectories all reading `cat /tmp/w/cups/usr/share/misc/magic.txt.5`, spanning 6 images, each holding a different canary — pool purity averages 62% same-read-command against a ~0.1% chance rate, with no pool containing a near-duplicate answer (max within-pool raw-768 cosine 0.98). Contract hygiene is clean on all counts I could execute: deterministic, no fit mutation, global RNG untouched, exactly bs in-range indices, 0.051 s setup and 113 us/batch on the real 2304-sequence fit. The partner-arch claim also holds exactly: r22 is bit-identical to r18 at init (all 101 shared parameters equal under the same seed, forward pred max abs diff 0.0). Where it diverges is in what the shipped parameters actually deliver. Two mechanisms the hypothesis presents as additive are in direct conflict, and at alpha_max=2.5 the depth tilt wins: late-phase batches collapse to 26 distinct sequences out of 64 with one sequence repeated ~19 times on average, which neutralizes the collision pools — same-read-command co-presence measured over distinct trajectories FALLS below uniform (2.21 groups/batch vs 8.09; mean largest group 2.80 vs 3.06), where at alpha=0 the same pools deliver exactly what the hypothesis describes (mean largest group 8.14, groups up to 17). The 117->636 figure only replicates if duplicate batch slots are counted, and a duplicate slot carries the same target, which is precisely not the "k different contents in one softmax" the argument rests on. Separately, the tilt overshoots the scored band: the eligible slice is depths {3,4} only, and the sampler spends 56% of draws (70% late-phase) at depth >= 5, with 1.5% of the corpus taking 51% of all draws — so "on the exact structure the eligible slice consists of" is not what is measured. The depth>=3 density claim (0.774) replicates almost exactly at 0.772, but its interior is not the eligible structure.

divergences.claim: "the collision pools force the name-keyed solution to be loss-bearing during training... When k trajectories whose read command is the same string sit in one batch, their k targets are different contents inside one softmax... On the same 960-sequence corpus the number of same-read-command pairs co-present in a batch goes from 117 (uniform) to 636."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The exp(alpha*z) depth tilt (batcher__r2_routedepth_tilt_readcollision_blocks.py:136-138) is applied INSIDE the collision pool, and multinomial draws are with replacement. At the genome's alpha_max=2.5 the tilt concentrates each 24-slot block onto the pool's one or two deepest members, so the pool of ~17 distinct trajectories collapses. Measured on the real encoded train split (2304 seqs, bs=64, 1200 steps, late phase = steps 601-1200): mean DISTINCT indices per batch 26.0 of 64; one sequence appears on average 19.5 times in a single batch (max 28 observed). Counting same-read-command co-presence over DISTINCT trajectories (which is what the argument requires — duplicate copies have the SAME target, not different contents), the number FALLS below uniform: 5.2 pairs/batch vs uniform 12.0; groups with >=2 distinct members 2.21/batch vs uniform 8.09; mean largest same-read-command group 2.80 vs uniform 3.06. The claimed mechanism is delivered only with the tilt off: at alpha_max=0 the same pools give mean largest group 8.14 with groups up to 17 distinct members. The two mechanisms the hypothesis presents as additive are in direct conflict, and the shipped configuration keeps the one that destroys the other. The 117->636 figure replicates only if duplicate batch SLOTS are counted as pairs (real split: 13.4 -> 270 slot-pairs per batch), and a duplicated slot is exactly not the counterfactual the argument invokes.

(17, 2) ... mean largest group 8.14`, `uniform ... mean largest group 3.06`. Stable across seeds 1/7/99: mean distinct/batch 25.8-26.2, mean max multiplicity 19.0-19.7.

divergences.claim: "Roughly a 1.9x increase in the density of depth-4-and-up routing examples per gradient step, at a fixed step budget, on the exact structure the eligible slice consists of."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The eligible scored slice is depths {3, 4} ONLY — research/compositional-selection-design.md:69 ("89 windows on the inner split ... with depths {3, 4} only") and :171 ("Earnable cells exist only at depths 3 and 4 ... depths 1, 2, 5, 6 and 7 have none"; deeper windows have a saturated ceiling and are filtered out before the depth floor). The shipped sampler puts the bulk of its mass ABOVE that band. Measured draw-depth histogram over the full 1200-step run: depth 3 = 9.1%, depth 4 = 11.7%, depth >= 5 = 56.4%; late phase: depth 3 = 5.9%, depth >= 5 = 69.8%, with the 14 depth-7 sequences alone taking ~40% of late-phase draws. The 34 sequences at depth >= 6 (1.5% of the corpus) receive 51.4% of all draws over the run. The >= thresholds the hypothesis reports (depth>=3, depth>=4) conceal this: the depth>=3 number itself replicates almost exactly (claimed 0.774, measured 0.772), but the composition inside it is dominated by depths that are analytically unscoreable, not by the depth-3 windows that are 60 of the 89 eligible.

divergences.claim: "The parent's batcher mechanism I keep is system blocking... It survives as one of the two block families below, and my sampler reduces exactly to it when alpha = 0."
divergences.what_the_code_does: It does not. At alpha_max=0 half of the blocks are still collision pools (coll_share=0.5, line 133/154), n_blocks=2 vs the parent's single image-union block, and the per-block image is drawn independently rather than as one union pool, so the RNG stream and the composition both differ. Executed comparison against the parent impl r6_sysblock_hardneg_curriculum with its archived params returns False, and still False even when forced to coll_share=0.0, n_blocks=1.
divergences.evidence: batcher__r2_routedepth_tilt_readcollision_blocks.py:130-162 vs evolve/chunks/batcher/r6_sysblock_hardneg_curriculum.py. Executed: `alpha=0 identical to parent r6 stream: False`; `alpha=0,coll=0,n_blocks=1 identical to parent: False`.

divergences.claim: "A uniform component ... is kept for the whole run so coverage of the corpus is never lost" and "The 25% uniform floor and the coverage figure above (959/960 distinct sequences touched) bound this."

divergences.claim: "read_at(sequence) = the step index attaining it" — implicitly the cups_test read; verified 24/24 against meta["cups"]["depth"].
divergences.what_the_code_does: The code computes the deepest routed read over ALL `cat` steps, which is exactly what the hypothesis's pseudocode says, and the 24/24 check reproduces exactly. On the wider real corpus the identification with the cups read is not universal: 164 of 2304 fit sequences (7.1%) have their deepest routed read on a /tmp/w/cvar/... path rather than a /tmp/w/cups/... path. On a fresh 400-sequence slice of the real train root the walk's depth equals the recorded cups depth in 395/400 (5 read depth 2 where cups depth is 1), and depth AND step index both match in 364/400. The difficulty measure is therefore ~99% faithful by value but the read_at used for the collision embeddings is a cvar read in ~7% of cases.
